description: FIRST MULTI-DISJOINT-LOOP CUT GOLDEN (a ring of lightening holes cut in ONE feature — showcase F2, docs/showcase-parts.md / BACKLOG #4): a 60 x 60 x 10 mm plate (rectangle sketch + additive extrude) is cut by a SECOND sketch of SIX disjoint r4 circles arranged on a ring of radius 20 about the plate centre (30, 30), with NO enclosing outer boundary, in a single subtractive extrude. Locks the CUT-only multi-region path of build_profile_faces: N disjoint closed loops -> _group_regions partitions them into N independent removal regions (each a bare loop here, no interior holes) -> N cut tools prism-extruded and subtracted from the running body in deterministic (_wire_sort_key) order -> one connected solid with 6 through-holes -> GProp -> curved-face tessellation of the 6 cylindrical hole walls -> content-addressed GLB. This is the CUT relaxation only: an ADD extrude of disjoint loops stays a multi-body profile_unsupported error (build_profile_face), and the single-outer-boundary plate-with-holes path is byte-unchanged for both add and cut.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). Outer plate x in [0,60], y in [0,60] on the XY datum plane (4 lines), extruded +10 mm (add) to a 60 x 60 x 10 block; six through-holes are full circles radius 4 whose centres sit at (30 + 20 cos(60k deg), 30 + 20 sin(60k deg)) for k = 0..5 — a ring of radius 20 about (30, 30). Adjacent hole centres are 2*20*sin(30 deg) = 20 mm apart, sum of radii 8 mm, so the six loops are mutually disjoint (no shared outer boundary — the case build_profile_face rejects and build_profile_faces accepts for a CUT). Each hole lies well inside the plate (nearest centre-to-edge 10 mm > r 4), so all six cut clean through without grazing the outer walls.

The sketch entities start at their analytic positions with no constraints (zero residual, DOF free), so planegcs returns the input positions bitwise — the same solver posture as the plate-with-holes golden.
volume = 60*60*10 - 6*(pi*4^2*10) = 36000 - 960*pi = 32984.0710525538 mm^3 (block 36000 minus six full cylindrical holes pi*16*10 = 160*pi each).

surface_area = 2*(3600 - 6*pi*4^2)  [top + bottom plate faces, each pierced by six holes]  + 4*60*10  [four outer side walls]  + 6*(2*pi*4*10)  [six cylindrical hole walls]  = (7200 - 192*pi) + 2400 + 480*pi = 9600 + 288*pi = 10504.778684233861 mm^2.

centroid = (30, 30, 5) mm: the six holes lie on a ring symmetric about the plate centre (30, 30) (their centres sum to (180, 180), mean (30, 30)), so removing them preserves the full-block centroid; extrude 'normal' on XY is +Z, z spans [0,10]. (GProp puts x/y at ulp scale ~2.1e-14 mm because the ring centres carry float-trig rounding; z exactly 5.)
bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[60,60,10]: the interior holes do not touch the outer boundary, so the AABB is the un-holed block's box (exact, driven by the four integer-coordinate rectangle lines).

topology: 12 faces (top + bottom plate faces, 4 outer side walls, 6 cylindrical hole walls), 30 edges (top boundary = 4 rect edges + 6 hole circles = 10; bottom = 10; 4 vertical box corner edges; 1 vertical seam edge on each of the 6 periodic hole cylinders = 6), 1 shell. A plate face bounded by an outer loop + six inner hole loops is still ONE face — the holes add faces/edges only through the six cylinder walls they cut. Cutting six disjoint tools in sequence leaves exactly one connected solid (each hole is interior, so no cut disconnects the block).

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular 0.1 rad, isRelative=False): each full hole circle discretizes to 2*ceil(2*pi/0.1) = 126 segments (the same 2x-angular rule the cylinder/plate-with-holes goldens exhibit; radius-independent at these sizes, where the 0.1 rad angular bound dominates the 0.1 mm linear bound). Six periodic hole cylinders = 6 * ((126+1)*2 nodes, 126*2 tris) = 1524 nodes / 1512 triangles. Each plate cap is a planar face with a rectangular outer loop (4 nodes) + six 126-gon holes = 4 + 6*126 = 760 boundary nodes, triangulated with holes to 760 - 2 + 2*6 = 770 triangles (no interior node); two caps = 1520 nodes / 1540 triangles. Four rectangular side walls = 4 * (4 nodes, 2 tris) = 16 nodes / 8 triangles. Totals = 1524 + 1520 + 16 = 3060 vertices and 1512 + 1540 + 8 = 3060 triangles (per-face faceted normals, no vertex sharing across faces — same convention as the box/cylinder/plate-with-holes goldens).

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: CURVED-GEOMETRY tolerance (six cylindrical hole walls), measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). The six SEQUENTIAL cut booleans plus the cylinders' Gauss-quadrature volume/surface integration in GProp accumulate ulp-scale error across the tools. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-13, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume 1.46e-11 mm^3, surface_area 3.64e-12 mm^2, centroid <= 2.14e-14 mm (x/y at ring float-trig ulp scale; z exactly), AABB exactly 0.0 on all six bounds. Documented ceiling 1e-9 = ~69x the observed worst case (volume), headroom for libm/platform variation across CI hosts while staying 100x TIGHTER than the standing planar 1e-7 bound, matching the extrude/cylinder/plate-with-holes goldens' posture. The multi-region partition and cut order are deterministic (_group_regions sorts by _wire_sort_key), and the solver contributes zero error by construction (zero-residual start, solved == input bitwise). Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
